//: Development only — ConfigurationSecretResolver allows a JSON-sourced secret here and
refuses it everywhere else (TR-SEC-28). Not a real key: generated with
openssl rand -base64 32 purely so `dotnet run` works locally with no extra setup.
DevelopmentAutoMigrate applies db/mssql at start-up and seeds the administrator below.
Ignored outside Development — DevelopmentBootstrapper checks the environment first, and
no configuration value can override that. UAT and Production use db/Deploy-Database.ps1.
DevelopmentAppUser supplies the $(AppUser) sqlcmd variable that 0008_permissions.sql
needs. Left unset that one script is skipped, which is usually what you want locally:
connecting as an administrator, CREATE USER ... FOR LOGIN fails because the login is
already mapped to dbo, and the GRANT/DENY rules would not apply to you anyway.
Local-only credentials. TR-SEC-28 forbids credentials in configuration outside
Development, and ConfigurationSecretResolver enforces that; here they are deliberate, so
that a fresh clone can sign in and exercise the UI with no manual setup.
The second factor is TOTP: the seeder logs an otpauth:// URI at start-up to add to an
authenticator app. The secret is fixed, so the entry keeps working across re-seeds.
